I’ve worked remotely on a computer for virtually my entire adult life, but somehow, finding a good desk has never been much of a priority. As long as I had a surface big enough for a laptop, it was usually good enough for me. In fact I often prioritized aesthetics and price for many years, meaning I often just used a vintage chair and table I found for cheap at an estate sale or thrift store. My most recent desk was quite literally just a piece of wood my husband attached to a wall. While all these desks have been perfectly functional, I wouldn’t have called the setups optimal. Now that I’m in my 40s, however, my body has started making it pretty clear that my makeshift workstations aren’t going to cut it forever. Apparently, ergonomics matter!

Thankfully, I was offered the Desky Dual Hardwood Sit Stand Desk and a Desky Evoque Low Back Office Chair just in the nick of time. I’ve only been using them for a couple of weeks, but I can confidently say that, for the first time in my life, I officially have a very good Grown-Up Desk setup. And, honestly? I’m not sure how I worked without one for so long.
What Is Desky’s Dual Hardwood Sit Stand Desk?

The Desky Dual Hardwood desk is an electric, height-adjustable desk with a modern look that lets you switch between sitting and standing throughout the workday. It combines a solid hardwood tabletop with a dual-motor steel frame, so adjusting the height is as simple as pressing a button. No need to guess at adjusting the heights; you can even program preset heights for your preferred sitting and standing positions, as well as settings for other people in your household. There’s also an app that allows you to adjust the desk from your phone.

Designed for not just looks but also stability, the desk can support up to 330 pounds and is astoundingly sturdy and heavy. Available in several hardwood finishes, including walnut, white ash, white oak, acacia, teak, and pheasantwood, it has the substantial feel and appearance of a high-end piece of furniture. Desky also offers optional wire management options to help corral the amount of wires required to be a working adult in today’s modern home.
What Is Desky’s Evoque Low Back Office Chair?

The Desky Evoque Low Back Office Chair is an ergonomic office chair with a more streamlined, design-forward appearance than traditional office chairs. It features a low back and a dynamic tilting function, and it comes in several color combinations. I opted for the dark green version, which has a vintage-inspired look that feels much more at home in a thoughtfully decorated room than a typical office chair. And while I initially chose the low-back design primarily for aesthetic reasons, I was pleasantly surprised by how comfortable it turned out to be.
How Building and Operating Desky’s Dual Hardwood Sit Stand Desk and Evoque Low Back Office Chair Went

Full confession: My wonderful husband assembled both the desk and chair before I even realized what was happening, so I can’t personally speak to every step of the process. He assured me, however, that assembly was straightforward and the instructions were easy to follow. The only tools required were the included wrench. The reason why he was able to assemble it so stealthily was because he didn’t utter a single curse word while building it. You should consider assembling the desk near where you’ll be permanently parking it — it’s heavy. I definitely could not have moved it by myself. One more thing worth mentioning: Both products arrive in a large number of boxes. For a moment, you’ll wonder whether you accidentally ordered two or three desks.

Installing and operating the Desky desk was a bit more difficult than assembling it, but not by much. The two steel legs have their own power cords, which connect to a control box, and there’s also wiring for the small control pad that operates the desk. I also ordered Desky’s Integrated Cable & Power Channel (with three plugs, one USB-C port, and one USB port; there are other options available), which added a few more cords to the equation. Between the desk’s power supply, the leg connections, my laptop charger, monitor, and internet equipment, my husband and I spent a few minutes figuring out the best way to organize everything.
Why I Love Desky’s Dual Hardwood Sit Stand Desk

I’m most impressed with how high-quality the materials are as well as the construction. I’m a beast to my work surfaces — tea spilling, paint splashes, gouges from dropping things — but this hardwood top and its finishing coat look brand-new even after a couple of weeks of constant daily use. Once I got the hang of giving the “up” button a slightly-firmer-than-expected press, adjusting the desk’s height was simple. I chose the White Ash top with the white steel legs, and I visually find that combo to be the perfect modern yet neutral base for my desktop decor.

Available in a number of different widths, the Desky’s 30” depth is more than ample for my laptop, monitor, mouse and more accouterments. I think for my household at least, I won’t be necessarily using the adjustable option on a daily basis — at 43 years of age I’m pretty content sitting while I work, but being able to adjust the height easily if and when my husband wants to come work on the desk is quite convenient. And I’ve found another use for it: standing while working on art and craft projects. The generous surface area makes it a great workspace for those activities, too.
Why I Love Desky’s Evoque Low Back Office Chair

I’ll be honest: I’m usually pretty allergic to the aesthetics of most ergonomic office chairs. But Desky’s Evoque Low back office chair reminded me of a sleek vintage-style chair. I ordered it in dark green, but it comes in nine additional color combos. I can safely say that it’s one of the most comfortable office chairs I’ve ever sat in. I was initially worried that choosing the low back for aesthetics would be a mistake, but I haven’t once wanted or needed a higher back as I’ve worked.

I also didn’t know that I was missing a dynamic tilting function in my office chair, but now that I’ve experienced it with this one I may never be able to go back. As someone with hypermobility, I’m constantly shifting around and finding somewhat unconventional positions to get comfortable. The chair’s tilting function makes that much easier. Sitting cross-legged is a little snug, but it’s doable, which is a win in my book.
Last Things to Consider Before Purchasing Desky’s Dual Hardwood Sit Stand Desk

There’s one thing I wish I’d thought about before deciding where to put my new desk: A height-adjustable desk needs room to actually adjust its height! This might seem obvious, but somehow it hadn’t occurred to me that the desk would need enough clearance above it to move freely. I live in an almost-100-year-old house with wooden window sills, which means I can’t push the desk completely against the wall or into the corner the way I originally wanted. It’s a small but important consideration, especially if you’re working with an older home or a room with low windows, shelves, or artwork above your desk. Before settling on a spot, measure the available vertical clearance and make sure nothing will get in the way when you raise the desk.

And while Desky does offer wire management products, I admit that I could still use more wire control. I should have counted exactly how many things I’d need to plug in alongside the Desky before ordering my add-ons. Between the Desky, my monitor, my laptop charger, my wireless router, along with a charger for my phone and my headphones (that I use daily), I still feel like there are more visible wires than I’d like. But, I consider that more poor planning on my part rather than a ding against Desky.
